q: What exchange is NQ on?
a: NQ is the E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures contract. It trades electronically on CME Globex under CME Group. Not a stock. Not Nasdaq cash. A CME-listed equity-index future.

q: What exchange is ES on?
a: ES is the E-mini S&P 500 futures contract. It also trades on CME Globex (CME Group). Same venue family as NQ. Different underlying index.

q: What does /ES or /NQ mean?
a: Slash notation is the continuous futures symbol used by many platforms and brokers. It points at the front-month (or roll-adjusted) series so you do not type a specific month every day. The actual tradable is still a dated contract (e.g. ESU6).

q: What are futures contract months (H M U Z)?
a: Equity-index E-minis use quarterly months: H March, M June, U September, Z December. Front month is the nearest liquid quarter until the roll. Always know which month your DOM and order ticket are on.

q: What is a tick and a point on ES / NQ?
a: On ES and NQ the minimum tick is 0.25 index points. One point = 4 ticks. ES: $12.50 per tick ($50 per point). NQ: $5 per tick ($20 per point). Micro contracts (/MES /MNQ) are one-tenth of those values.

q: What is CME Globex?
a: Globex is CME Group's electronic trading platform. Nearly all modern ES/NQ/CL retail and prop volume prints there. Pit lore is history. Your feed is Globex electronic matching.

q: What is the difference between the cash index and the futures?
a: The Nasdaq-100 or S&P 500 cash index is a calculated number from stocks. NQ/ES are tradable futures that price expectations of that index plus cost-of-carry and overnight inventory. Gaps and overnight moves live in futures first.

q: What is a micro futures contract?
a: MES and MNQ are micro E-minis — roughly 1/10 the notional and tick dollar value of ES/NQ. Same Globex venue and auction. Smaller risk unit for learning and sized practice. Not a different market law.

q: What is ETH / electronic trading hours?
a: ETH means Electronic Trading Hours — the Globex overnight / extended session outside the primary cash open block. For equity index futures that is most of the 23-hour Globex day outside RTH. Liquidity is thinner; inventory and news still move price.

q: What is RTH / regular trading hours?
a: RTH for US equity-index futures is the primary daytime cash session window — commonly about 09:30–16:00 Eastern for ES/NQ cash-aligned activity (desk labels vary slightly; lock yours). Most retail volume and many play criteria reference RTH.

q: When does Globex trade ES / NQ?
a: Nearly around the clock Sunday evening through Friday, with a short daily maintenance break (commonly around 16:00–17:00 Eastern — confirm current CME schedule). Weekend closed. Hours change; verify CME before you assume.

q: What is overnight inventory?
a: Positions and price path built during ETH relative to the prior RTH close. The RTH open often reacts to where overnight left the auction — not to a magic gap-fill script. Inventory informs context; it is not a signal.

q: What does session mean in this course?
a: A locked time window you journal against — usually RTH for Track A plays, with ETH as context. Do not change the definition mid-week to excuse a trade. Consistency beats clever labels.

q: What is a market order?
a: A market order says: take liquidity now at whatever price is offered or bid. You pay the spread and any slip. You do not pick a price — the book picks you. Useful when you must be in; expensive when you are lazy.

q: What is a limit order?
a: A limit order rests at your price (or better). It may not fill. You control worst price; you do not control fill certainty. At the open across a gap, resting limits behave by exchange matching rules — they do not magically become the gap print.

q: How do you see market orders executing?
a: On ATAS: Smart Tape / Time & Sales shows prints; Clusters (Bid×Ask) show aggression at price; DOM shows depth changing as marketable orders lift offers or hit bids. Market orders consume resting liquidity. That consumption is what you read as aggression.

q: What does lifting the offer / hitting the bid mean?
a: Lifting the offer = buy marketable (take ask). Hitting the bid = sell marketable (take bid). That is aggression. Passive size rests. Footprint Bid×Ask language is built on this.

q: What are opening gaps?
a: An opening gap is when RTH opens away from the prior RTH close (or your locked reference print), leaving a price void on the RTH chart. Futures often already traded that path overnight on Globex — the gap is relative to the session you chart.

q: What caused a gap up or gap down?
a: Usually overnight inventory plus news, macro prints, earnings clusters, geopolitical headlines, or simply aggressive repositioning while cash was closed. The cause is information and orders — not a pattern name. Name the driver when you can; admit when you cannot.

q: How is the gap price made?
a: The open print is the first matched trades of the RTH session (or your defined open) after overnight Globex continuous trading. Indicative opens and call auctions on some products differ; for CME equity-index futures the overnight book already priced discovery. The gap on your RTH chart is arithmetic between prior close and that open — not mystical ink from nowhere.

q: What is auction theory in plain words?
a: Markets discover price by buyers and sellers showing size and aggression. Balance = accepted value. Imbalance = price seeks new value. Profiles and footprints are maps of that auction — not crystal balls.

q: Do limit orders miss or get filled at open price across a gap?
a: It depends on order type, side, and matching. A buy limit below a gap-up open typically does not fill at the open — price is already above your limit. A sell limit above a gap-down open often misses the open print the same way. Stop-markets can fill worse through the void. Limits do not catch the gap price just because you wanted them to. Read your broker's open/gap handling; do not assume YouTube rules.

q: What is the market must fill the gap theory — and why we do not treat it as law?
a: Retail folklore says price must return to fill every gap. Sometimes price revisits; sometimes it never does for a long time; sometimes it fills much later with no edge for you today. Gaps are session artefacts and overnight auctions — not IOUs from the market. We note unfilled gaps as context. We do not treat gap-fill as a mandatory trade or a law of nature.

q: What are HFT firms?
a: High-frequency trading firms use co-located servers, fast market data, and automated strategies to trade large volumes of small edges — market making, arb, short-horizon speculation. They are participants in the book. They are not a cartoon villain under your bed. You will not beat their ping from a home Wi-Fi hero story.

q: What is low latency?
a: Low latency means short delay between event, decision, and order reach to the matching engine. Measured in microseconds to milliseconds for pros. Your edge as a discretionary student is criteria and risk — not racing HFT. Clean feed and stable connection still matter so your screen is not a lie.

q: What is M1 and M2 money supply?
a: M1 and M2 are Federal Reserve monetary aggregates. M1 is the narrow stack — currency and checkable/near-checkable deposits (definitions revised over time; use current Fed tables). M2 is broader — M1 plus savings-like deposits and retail money-market funds (again: check current Fed composition). They measure money-like balances in the banking system. They are not a secret switch for next week's NQ print.

q: What is the platform stack in this course?
a: ATAS is the classroom: Clusters Bid×Ask, Delta/CVD, Volume Profile, Smart Tape/DOM, Market Replay. CQG Integrated Client is what Chris uses personally to execute — you do not need it to learn. TradingView is context only — not tick footprint truth.

q: What is a footprint / cluster chart in ATAS?
a: Volume traded at each price inside a bar, usually Bid×Ask or delta per price. Shows imbalance, unfinished auctions, and absorption detail candles hide. In ATAS this is Clusters — Bid×Ask primary for this curriculum.

q: What is Bid×Ask on the cluster?
a: At each price, volume traded on the bid vs the ask. Ask-side volume approximates buy aggression (lifted offers). Bid-side volume approximates sell aggression (hit bids). Know your ATAS colour/layout. This is the alphabet — not a buy arrow.

q: What is CVD?
a: Cumulative Volume Delta — running sum of buying vs selling aggression (delta) over the session or chosen period. Sustained CVD and divergences are evidence layers — not magic arrows. ATAS carries delta/CVD as a question engine.

q: What is a volume profile?
a: Volume at price for a session (or range). Shows where the auction did business. Nodes (HVN/LVN) and value area (VAH/VAL/POC) are location tools for criteria — not crystal balls. ATAS: Fixed and Developing profiles.

q: What size bands does Stage 3 use?
a: Clean plays (1–2): about 0.25–0.75% capital risk. Event plays (3): 0.10–0.50%. Marginal criteria means cut size or stand aside. Stop distance drives contract count.

q: How do I turn risk percent into contracts on /ES?
a: Risk dollars = account times risk percent. Tick value times stop ticks = dollar risk per contract. Contracts = floor(risk dollars / dollars per contract). Never round up to feed ego. Same math on NQ with NQ tick value.

q: What is R-multiple?
a: R is your planned risk on the trade (entry to invalidation in dollars). +2R means you made twice planned risk. Journal in R so ego dollars do not rewrite the story.

q: What is max daily loss for?
a: A hard stop on the day so one spiral does not erase a month. Hit it — flat — journal. Not a suggestion. Lifestyle OS and Stage 0 treat this as standard, not soft advice.

q: Is stand aside really an edge?
a: Yes. Flat is a position. Most missed winners were correctly avoided losers in disguise. Process score rewards correct flats.

q: What is Stage 0 and do I need it before footprint?
a: Stage 0 is Non-Retail Starter — standards, risk basics, Lifestyle OS, Constitution, gate. Yes. No footprint / CVD / profile stack until the gate clears. Toys after standards.

q: What is the Stage 0 gate checklist?
a: Binary: Execute work 0.0–0.6 done; Trading + Life Constitution signed and dated; gate affidavit signed; data is king logged and indicator stack audited. Vibes do not clear the gate.

q: I bought Futures access. Can I skip Starter?
a: If Stage 0 was not cleared, you still clear the gate. Paying for Track A does not delete process. Soft care: if you are trying, finish the foundation — we do not lower the bar.

q: What should I put in the trade journal?
a: Play code, ALL criteria score, size, invalidation hit?, stand aside?, body check, one lesson. Replay gate before size-up. Honesty beats pretty screenshots.

q: Why is there a body check before session?
a: Body is part of the risk system. Sleep, food, alcohol rules, gym — Stage 0 Lifestyle OS. Optional 60s pre-session body check in Stages 1–3. Fail the body check means cut size or flat.

q: Is alcohol really a program rule?
a: Yes in-program: no alcohol. Not a vibe suggestion. Consumption mastery is part of the Constitution thread. Health is number one wealth.

q: What is Non-Retail Starter vs Non-Retail Futures?
a: Starter (£97) is Stage 0. Non-Retail Futures is the flagship (Track A intraday first; Track B Swing later) including Stages 1+. No signals in either. Starter Snap Cards slice = Stage 0 + basics; full Futures unlocks full bank.

q: Will you send trade signals?
a: No. Never. Criteria teach. We do not ping entries. If you came for a tip service, wrong room.

q: What is soft care in this course?
a: Hard line on truth; soft care for the man who is trying. Pattern line: If you are trying, this is for you. I will not lower the bar — I will help you clear it. Once max per piece.

q: Do I have to gym daily?
a: Daily gym is a program standard — train the body that sits the risk. Adapt for injury with honesty, not laziness cosplay.

q: What does See: mean on a Snap Card?
a: Pointer to lesson or play code for deeper work. Snap Cards are truth plus revision — not a replacement for the lesson film or play card.

q: Is gap must fill a market law?
a: No. It is a common belief and a sometimes-useful map note. Price often revisits; often it does not on your timetable. We do not treat gap-fill as mandatory edge. See SNAP-0037.

q: What does data is king mean here?
a: Transactions, size at price, aggression vs absorption, session location — not oscillator soup. TA that decorates after the auction decided is retail theatre.

q: Is this financial advice?
a: No. Education only. Futures trading involves substantial risk of loss. You are responsible for your decisions and compliance with local rules.

q: What is Process · Knowledge · Execution?
a: Program spine. Stage 0 process/standards; Stage 1 knowledge/reading; Stage 2 context; Stage 3 execution. Retail usually dies at execution while collecting vocabulary.

q: How does Snap Cards separate Zell from fakers?
a: Locked answers. No invented signals. Futures-first ATAS classroom. Soft care sparingly. Explicit anti-theatre category. You search a named question and get blunt truth — not a webinar funnel.

q: What is margin in futures (concept)?
a: Performance bond — good-faith deposit, not the full notional. Exchange/broker set initial and maintenance margins. Leverage cuts both ways. Concept literacy; your broker's numbers rule.

q: What is a micro contract for in practice?
a: Smaller tick/notional so risk percent maps to fewer dollars while you build process. Not a toy forever — a sizing tool. Ego that 'only standards count' often skips Stage 0 maths.

q: Why does RTH still matter if Globex is near 24h?
a: RTH concentrates US cash equity related flow, tighter typical liquidity for indices, and the open auction. ETH still matters for inventory. Knowing both beats living in one timezone story.

q: Multi-timezone life — how do UK traders think about US RTH?
a: US RTH is afternoon/evening in UK. Sleep and food matter more than 'grind culture'. If you are wrecked at the open, stand aside. Body is part of the session plan.

q: R-multiple — deepen the idea?
a: 1R = initial risk planned. Outcomes in R let you compare trades across size. +2R on micro and +2R on full size are the same process score, different dollars. Journal in R.

q: How does sleep hit trading decisions?
a: Sleep debt raises impulsivity and shrinks patience for stand-aside. You will invent criteria. Body check includes sleep. Tired + markets = voluntary tuition.

q: Gym as training metaphor — what does Zell mean?
a: Reps under load. Progressive standards. No highlight-reel ego. Missed days compound. Trading process is trained the same way — boring consistency beats inspirational spikes.

q: What is the grow-up moment in this program?
a: When you stop collecting setups and start keeping standards — body, journal, risk, stand-aside — without an audience. Grow up. All in on process. Not on cosplay.

q: Myth: the market must fill the gap — kill it again?
a: Gaps often fill over some horizon — and often do not on your timetable. Treating fill as law creates forced fades and ignored inventory. See SNAP-0037 / 0096. Belief ≠ edge.

q: How should students audit a 'funded success' story?
a: Ask: time window, number of attempts/fees, risk rules used, post-pass expectancy, journal standards, losing streaks shown. If answers are vibes, treat as ad.

q: Zell filter: when is a prop/tool worth considering?
a: When you can state rules in one paragraph, size without fantasy, journal without screenshots, and accept stand-aside. Tool serves process. If process is missing, the tool is a costume.

q: How do you pre-commit against tilt?
a: Written max daily loss, max trades, size ladder, stand-aside triggers (sleep, alcohol, family stress), and a kill switch: platform logout. Pre-commit when calm. Enforce when hot.

q: What should a trading journal actually contain?
a: Setup name/criteria score, size/risk R, entry/exit reason, invalidation, session context, emotion/tilt tags, screenshot of the decision board — not just PnL. Stand-asides count as entries.

q: What is a pre-session checklist card?
a: Sleep, body, calendar, platform health, max loss, plays in play, stand-aside triggers. Tick before size. Red tick → no trade.

q: ATAS advanced — what stays Stage-1 sacred?
a: Replay, fail galleries, naming behaviours, linking to plays later. Live size still waits for criteria and Stage gates. Advanced eyes without Stage 0 is expensive cosplay.

q: What is the Initial Balance (IB) in plain language?
a: Usually the range established in the first hour of the cash session (definitions vary — know yours). IB is a reference for later expansion or balance — not a crystal ball.

q: How should UK-based traders map US day structure?
a: Translate clocks: IB, midday, power hour in London time. Protect sleep. Do not force Asia heroics because you are awake.

q: Sim vs live — what actually changes?
a: Psychology, slippage, partial fills, queue priority, hesitation. Sim is for reps and eyes. Live is for criteria under consequence. Treating sim PnL as proof is theatre.

q: How do you write a swing thesis (non-signal)?
a: One paragraph: directional bias, why (structure/context), invalidation level/condition, time horizon, news risks, size as fraction of day-risk book. No entry spam. Thesis is a contract with yourself.

q: What is sleep debt as trading risk?
a: Debt compounds: slower processing, emotional reactivity, FOMO susceptibility. You cannot caffeine your way into clean criteria forever. Sleep is risk infrastructure.

q: Why Zell ties health to trading gospel?
a: Because decision variance is physiological. Consumption, sleep, training — these are risk tools. Aesthetic wellness is optional. Function is not.

q: Glossary: What is retail theatre?
a: Performance sold as trading education: signals, cropped curves, FOMO funnels, costume dashboards. Snap Cards exist to filter it.
